title: Biased output pivotal probability
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p\in(0,1)$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $b\in\{\pm1\}$, and let $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The biased output pivotal probability of $f$ for output $b$ at coordinate $i$ is the probability, when the input coordinates are independently drawn from the $p$-biased sign distribution, that changing coordinate $i$ can change the output from $b$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on $n$ sign coordinates
caveat: The referenced predicate IsOutputPivotal is not defined in the supplied snippet, so its exact meaning cannot be established from the ground truth shown.
